item.title: Delhi under siege as 6,000 detained in election protests
item.description:
Around 6,000 people were detained across New Delhi yesterday as Indian authorities imposed sweeping security restrictions to prevent a major protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, triggering a political confrontation over electoral integrity and the right to peaceful assembly.
Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, student leaders, activists, lawyers and prominent online personalities were among those detained as thousands of police and paramilitary personnel effectively sealed off central Delhi.
The unprecedented security operation prevented protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar, where the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had called a mass demonstration against alleged manipulation of electoral rolls.
According to The Indian Express, around 6,000 people had been detained by 7pm, although police began releasing some detainees later in the evening.
The crackdown followed weeks of demonstrations over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has seen approximately 130 million names removed from draft voter lists across 30 states and Union Territories.
Opposition parties allege that the exercise has disenfranchised eligible voters and favoured Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the ruling party deny the allegations.
Mamata Banerjee was detained alongside several Trinamool Congress lawmakers after staging a sit-in near the South Avenue bus stand when police prevented them from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar.
Among those detained with her were Derek O’Brien, Dola Sen, Saket Gokhale and Pratima Mondal.
Banerjee later alleged that police had forcibly placed them in a detention van and driven them between police stations for nearly two hours.
She said the experience left them feeling as though they had been kidnapped.
Kejriwal, the Aam Aadmi Party leader, was also detained while attempting to join the demonstration. He was released from Jafarpur Kalan police station in the evening.
Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, activist Yogendra Yadav, Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan and All India Students’ Association president Neha Bora were among others detained.
Police also detained prominent YouTuber Dhruv Rathee from his residence in Gurugram, according to Indian media reports.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and fellow organisers Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained inside an aircraft shortly after arriving in Delhi from Mumbai.
Their detention prompted the movement to appoint Ajinkya Shinde to coordinate yesterday’s protests.
With senior organisers unable to reach the demonstration site, protesters attempted to regroup at several locations across the capital.
The authorities deployed around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel, erected extensive barricades and imposed restrictions on public transport ahead of the demonstration.
Forty-five metro stations remained closed yesterday evening, while mobile internet services were suspended within a four-kilometre radius of the protest area.
Long-distance train services were also disrupted, and police established checkpoints along major roads and entry routes into the capital.
Jantar Mantar, normally a designated site for demonstrations, was surrounded by security forces before protesters could assemble.
As a result, smaller demonstrations emerged around Connaught Place, Gurdwara Bangla Sahib, Dilli Haat, INA Market and other locations.
Police repeatedly dispersed gatherings and transported detainees to police stations, stadiums and temporary holding facilities.
The authorities said the demonstration had not been authorised because organisers failed to submit their application within the required notice period and had violated conditions imposed during previous protests.
Prohibitory orders were also enforced under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
Protest organisers rejected the restrictions, arguing that peaceful assembly was a constitutional right.
Police reported that six personnel were injured during disturbances, including incidents of alleged stone-pelting. The circumstances of the injuries were being investigated.
The security measures also drew scrutiny from India’s Supreme Court.
On Friday, a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned the blanket restrictions on metro and railway services, observing that public-order measures must remain proportionate.
The court called for the restrictions to be reconsidered and for essential public transport to operate under appropriate regulation.
Despite the intervention, extensive restrictions remained in place during Saturday’s demonstrations.
The Supreme Court Bar Association separately sought intervention over the detention of lawyers, including women advocates, who had attempted to join the protests.
The crackdown also drew criticism from international rights organisations.
Amnesty International called for the release of people detained solely for exercising their rights to expression and peaceful assembly.
The Committee to Protect Journalists urged authorities to release detained journalists and allow reporters to cover the protests without interference.
At the centre of the confrontation is a controversy over India’s electoral-roll revision process.
The SIR exercise, launched in Bihar in June 2025 and subsequently expanded, is intended to identify duplicate entries, deceased voters and people no longer eligible to remain on electoral rolls.
However, opposition parties argue that the process has resulted in the wrongful exclusion of eligible voters.
The controversy intensified after a September 23 investigation by The Indian Express revealed that two election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had recorded objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions concerning voter registration, deletions, appeals and electoral-roll software.
The investigation reported that some decisions had been taken without the commissioners’ knowledge or approval.
The Election Commission acknowledged the existence of the notes but described them as part of its internal decision-making process, maintaining that its formal decisions were unanimous.
The BJP also rejected accusations of electoral manipulation.
On October 6, BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said the 130 million names removed from draft rolls included approximately 28 million deceased voters, 63 million people who had shifted residence, 10 million duplicate entries and 30 million people who could not be traced.
The party stressed that removals from draft rolls did not necessarily represent final exclusions.
Amid the controversy, the Election Commission ordered special enrolment drives in states where the revision had been completed to help eligible voters whose names were left out.
Nevertheless, the dispute has continued to fuel nationwide protests.
An India Today analysis found 278 demonstrations concerning the Election Commission across 26 states between late September and October 2.
The BJP defended yesterday’s police operation, accusing opposition parties of encouraging disorder.
Party spokesperson Sambit Patra described the protest as unsuccessful, while Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta accused opposition leaders of attempting to disrupt public life.

item.title: Blast reported at Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh Airport
item.description:
King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh was evacuated Saturday after a blast was reported, witnesses and local officials told several news agencies.
A Saudi official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told the Associated Press that many people were wounded after a missile hit a passenger terminal. Saudi authorities have not yet issued a public statement.
The AFP news agency also reported that a number of people were injured, citing a local medical source who also spoke on the condition of anonymity.
“ER doctors are being called to hospitals across Riyadh,” the source told AFP. “We were told we are dealing with a ‘serious emergency situation.’ Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh.”
Several Western embassies in Riyadh, including those of Germany, Canada and Spain, urged citizens to avoid the airport.
Spain’s embassy referred to a “new attack” by the Houthi rebels in Yemen while Canada’s embassy warned of ongoing military activity.”
The reports come amid intensified fighting between Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed government in Yemen.
The Iran-backed Houthis have been launching strikes on targets in Saudi Arabia, including several this week on the airport in Riyadh that killed four people, injured several others, and damaged planes.
Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways canceled multiple flights between their ​respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday. Kuwait Airways also cancelled its flights on Saturday.
There was no immediate Houthi statement about the reported blast on Saturday.
Last month, Houthi rebels made advances on important strategic locations along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, with a Saudi-led coalition providing air support for Yemeni government forces seeking to take back those gains.
The Houthis have responded by launching attacks into Saudi Arabia, which represents a significant escalation in their multi-year conflict with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government after a peace deal unraveled in July.
The Saudi-backed government in Yemen last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, especially those around the Bab al-Mandab strait.

item.title: Bollywood actor Imran Khan detained during CJP protest in Mumbai
item.description:
Bollywood actor Imran Khan and his girlfriend Lekha Washington were among more than 400 people detained by Mumbai Police on Saturday during a protest in support of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) call for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The detentions took place at August Kranti Maidan, the proposed venue for the demonstration, and other locations across the city as police moved to prevent unauthorized gatherings.
Speaking to the media before his detention, Imran said he had joined the protest in his capacity as a citizen, seeking answers over restrictions on freedom of movement and the suppression of public voices.
“I don’t have demands. I am here as a citizen, as someone who lives in this city. I am here to see why freedom of movement is being restricted — why people’s voices are being suppressed. That is why I am here,” the actor said, according to ANI.
He clarified that he was not affiliated with any organization and was participating in his individual capacity.
“I don’t have any right to demand anything from people. I am not a part of any organization. I will stand as a representative,” he added.
Following his detention, Imran shared a photograph of himself apparently inside a police vehicle on social media, captioning it: “Apparently I’m going for a drive.”
The police action in Mumbai came amid a wider crackdown on demonstrations linked to the CJP’s protest call.
In New Delhi, around 1,000 protesters had been detained while attempting to march towards Jantar Mantar, Delhi Police sources said on Saturday.
The protesters were demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged voter roll irregularities and claims of “vote theft” raised by opposition groups.

item.title: Finance and Planning Minister unveils Walton solar ecosystem
item.description:
Walton has achieved a significant milestone in sustainable industrial development by introducing an integrated solar energy ecosystem aimed at expanding renewable energy use, improving energy efficiency, reducing carbon emissions and promoting environment friendly manufacturing.
The newly unveiled Walton Solar Ecosystem integrates solar power generation, energy storage, electricity supply to the national grid and the operation of household electrical and electronic appliances through a comprehensive solar-based technological system.
As part of this initiative, Walton has established rooftop and floating solar power projects at its manufacturing facilities, achieving a combined solar power generation capacity of 32 megawatts (MW), which the company says is equivalent to the total electricity demand of a large district town in Bangladesh.
A substantial portion of the electricity generated is used in Walton’s manufacturing operations, helping reduce energy costs. In addition, the company supplies approximately 1,150 megawatt-hours (MWh) of solar electricity annually to the national grid through the net metering system.
Beyond generating environmentally friendly solar electricity, Walton has developed and manufactured a wide range of solar-compatible and energy-efficient products, including solar panels, inverters, batteries and household appliances for air conditioning, food preservation, entertainment, cooking, lighting and laundry.
The Walton Solar Ecosystem was officially unveiled on Saturday (October 10, 2026), at a ceremony held at Walton Corporate Office in Bashundhara, Dhaka. Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury attended the event as the chief guest and formally inaugurated the integrated solar technology initiative.
Among those present were Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC Chairman S M Shamsul Alam, Vice-Chairman S M Ashraful Alam, Managing Director S M Mahbubul Alam and Directors S M Rezaul Alam, S M Monjurul Alam Ovee and Tahmina Afrose Tanna.
Following the inauguration, the finance minister visited the Walton Solar Ecosystem exhibition and inspected various products, including solar panels, solar power cables, energy storage inverters and batteries, solar hybrid refrigerators, air conditioners and smart televisions, as well as solar-powered washing machines, electric cookers, ovens, rice cookers, BLDC fans, solar-based pedestal and table fans, LED bulbs and street lights.
The Minister expressed satisfaction after learning about the advanced technologies and energy-saving features of these products. He particularly appreciated Walton’s efforts to introduce hybrid air conditioners, refrigerators and smart televisions capable of operating through a combination of solar power and conventional grid electricity, creating new opportunities for energy savings.
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury said, “Solar power is an environmentally friendly source of electricity. What Walton is doing with solar technology is something that is expected to expand across Bangladesh. Over the next one or two years, the country is expected to generate a substantial amount of electricity from solar energy. This will help meet people’s electricity needs at lower costs.
“Solar power will also reduce our dependence on imported fuels, save valuable foreign currency and strengthen our energy independence. Solar energy can be used not only for lighting but also to operate refrigerators, air conditioners, washing machines, ovens and a wide range of other electronic appliances. We hope people across the country will increasingly adopt solar energy solutions,” the finance minister added.
Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC Chairman S M Shamsul Alam said, “The Walton Solar Ecosystem will play an important role in helping customers reduce electricity bills, expanding the use of renewable energy, lowering carbon emissions and contributing to the development of a greener and more self-reliant Bangladesh.”
Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC Vice-Chairman S M Ashraful Alam said, “The Walton Solar Ecosystem is an integrated technological solution that combines environmentally friendly solar power generation, energy storage and electricity supply to the national grid with our capability to manufacture solar-powered household appliances.
“This initiative will create new business opportunities for Walton. Our objective is to further strengthen the company’s financial capacity and fundamental business position while creating sustainable, long-term value for investors in the capital market,” he added.
Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC Managing Director S M Mahbubul Alam said, “The Walton Solar Ecosystem is an integrated technological framework for generating, storing and efficiently utilizing solar electricity. Our ambition goes beyond ‘Made in Bangladesh’. We want to innovate and develop advanced technologies in Bangladesh and demonstrate the country’s technological capabilities in the global market.”
He further expressed the view that Walton’s development and manufacturing of renewable energy-based, environmentally friendly technological products under its Solar Ecosystem initiative would take the technological excellence, progress and capabilities of Bangladesh’s high-tech industry to new heights.
Officials at the event explained that Walton’s Solar Ecosystem incorporates hybrid technology that enables air conditioners, refrigerators and smart televisions to operate using solar electricity. Under sufficient sunlight conditions, compatible Walton hybrid refrigerators, air conditioners and smart televisions can run directly on solar power without requiring battery storage.
When the available solar electricity is insufficient to meet the appliances’ power requirements, the system automatically draws the additional electricity needed from the national grid. This hybrid operation allows consumers to reduce grid electricity consumption depending on solar power availability.
Walton has also integrated new models of washing machines, electric cookers and ovens into its Solar Ecosystem through Energy Storage System (ESS) technology.
Electricity generated by solar panels during the day can be stored in batteries and used later for various household activities. The integrated energy storage system can support the operation of washing machines, electric cookers, microwave ovens, rice cookers, BLDC fans and other household appliances.
Walton’s inverter and battery systems incorporate both solar and AC charging facilities, allowing batteries to be charged using either solar electricity or conventional grid power.
As part of the Walton Solar Ecosystem, the company has introduced an intelligent backup power supply system in its new Takyon e-bike models. Equipped with a smart, environmentally friendly and multipurpose energy solution, the advanced battery technology can transform an e-bike into a mobile energy storage system. This innovation combines electric mobility, solar energy storage and emergency backup power supply capabilities in a single integrated solution.
Walton has also introduced specialized photovoltaic (PV) solar cables designed to ensure safe and reliable electricity transmission within solar energy systems. These cables are engineered to withstand ultraviolet (UV) radiation, moisture and challenging environmental conditions. Featuring flexible tinned copper conductors and specialized insulation materials, Walton’s solar cables are designed to provide safe, durable and long-lasting electrical connections for solar power installations.

item.title: Rizvi: BNP to act as sleepless sentinels at Durga Puja mandaps
item.description:
BNP leaders and activists will act as volunteers and sleepless sentinels at every Durga Puja mandap across the country, to ensure the safe and uninterrupted celebration of the festival by members of the Hindu community, BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said on Saturday.
“They will act as volunteers and sentinels at every Puja mandap like sleepless guards,” he said.
Rizvi made the remarks while briefing reporters after a meeting of the BNP’s highest policymaking body, the National Standing Committee, chaired by BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday night.
The meeting began at 6:30pm at the BNP chairman’s office in Gulshan in the capital.
Rizvi said the meeting primarily discussed ensuring the safe and uninterrupted celebration of Durga Puja across the country, allowing members of the Hindu community to take part in the festivities and share their joy with others.
The party leaders discussed how BNP activists would coordinate with local Puja committees at different mandaps across the country and perform voluntary duties to help ensure security during the festival, he said.
“You know that various kinds of blueprints are being drawn by some quarters against the country and the democratic government,” Rizvi said.
He expressed hope that the government would be able to thwart all kinds of propaganda, misdeeds and conspiracies through efficient management and administration, adding that BNP leaders and activists would remain vigilant in this regard.
He said the meeting also discussed what steps could be taken on the issue and what the party had already done.
Rizvi said the BNP had formed a central Durga Puja monitoring committee on Friday under the leadership of Joint Secretary Generals Khairul Kabir Khokon and Syed Emran Saleh Prince, he added.
The party had also issued various instructions earlier to ensure the peaceful celebration of the festival, he said.
“We are deeply concerned about this issue, and all of us remain alert,” Rizvi said.
The meeting also discussed organisational matters, including the party’s future course of action and ways to further intensify its organisational activities, Rizvi said.
He said there was no discussion at the meeting about the upcoming local government elections.
Asked whether there was any message regarding the formation of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) committee, Rizvi said no such message had reached him so far that he could share with the media.
He also confirmed that the party’s national council was not discussed at the meeting.
Those present at the meeting included Gayeshwar Chandra Roy MP, Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Selima Rahman, Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Power and Energy Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmood Tuku, Social Welfare Minister Prof AZM Zahid Hossain, Amanullah Aman MP, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Public Administration Ismail Zabiullah, and BNP Chairman’s Adviser Dr Farhad Halim Doner.

item.title: Army urges public not to be misled by propaganda targeting force, chief
item.description:
The Bangladesh Army has warned against the circulation of misleading, baseless and malicious information involving the force and the army chief on various online platforms and social media.
The army said such propaganda appears aimed at confusing the public and tarnishing its image.
The warning came in a press release published on the Bangladesh Army’s verified Facebook page on Saturday.
The release said the army had recently noticed the spread of misleading and deliberate information involving the force and its chief on various online platforms and social media.
It also shared links to several Facebook posts and YouTube videos as examples of the alleged misinformation.
The army urged people not to be influenced by such misleading and malicious propaganda.
It said the Bangladesh Army remains united through a strong chain of command, mutual trust, unity, discipline and professionalism, and is firmly committed to fulfilling its responsibilities to the country and its people.
The army also urged the public to verify information concerning the force or its chief through official and reliable sources.

item.title: Bangladeshi youth reportedly injured in BSF firing along Jhenaidah border
item.description:
A Bangladeshi youth was reportedly injured in firing by India's Border Security Force (BSF) along the Maheshpur border in Jhenaidah on Saturday.
The injured is Ujjal Hossain, 30, son of Harun-or-Rashid of Mailbaria Paschimpara village under Nepa Union in Maheshpur upazila.
According to locals and border sources, Ujjal was allegedly attempting to cross into India illegally around noon when patrolling BSF personnel from the Pakhuria camp under Hanskhali police station in India's Nadia district opened fire on him.
He sustained a bullet injury, reportedly from a rubber bullet, and was quickly rescued by relatives and associates, who took him away from the border area for secret treatment, the sources said.
BGB-58 Battalion (Maheshpur) Deputy Commander Munshi Imdadur Rahman said a special BGB patrol team was sent to Ujjal's house to investigate, but family members denied that any firing had taken place.
BGB surveillance and inquiries were continuing to establish what had happened along the border and whether anyone had been injured, he added.

item.title: Subsidize people, not things
item.description:
If poor people don't have enough money, then the solution is to give some money to the poor people. Then they will have more money and so, depending upon how much we give them, the poor people will have enough money.
This is a simple solution which, sadly, all too much of politics refuses to understand.
This is also the solution that the World Bank insists would be right for Bangladesh .
Give the subsidy, the money, to the poor people. Don't subsidize a thing that some poor people use or need. Because people who are not poor will also get that subsidy on that thing. The way to make sure that the subsidy actually goes to those who are poor is to subsidize poor people, not things.
For example, there's a subsidy for fertilizer. But there are rich farmers as well as poor ones. As it happens, rich farmers -- because they're rich -- tend to have more land than poor ones. More land means more fertilizer use. So, richer farmers get more of the fertilizer subsidy than poorer ones do -- they use more of the subsidised fertilizer.
There are subsidies for electricity and those too are captured by those richer than the very poorest. The very poor use less electricity because they're very poor. It's richer people who have more electricity consuming equipment, so it's richer people who get more of the electricity subsidy.
That's not what we're trying to do with these subsidies. We want to make the poor better off. But any, and every, system of subsidy of things will suffer from the same problem. So, the answer is simple: Do not subsidize things, subsidize people.
Poverty relief should -- should, note -- mean giving money to poor people. Not constructing systems of subsidy for things.
There are other problems with the subsidy of things. India's system of subsidized rations for the very poor each month is well known for never actually reaching the relevant people: It's all been stolen, or gone rotten, long before it reaches them.
But there's another, more theoretical problem. Not everyone wants the same thing. For example, we have poor people who are not farmers. So, the money we spend upon fertilizer subsidies is still public money being spent upon poverty alleviation, but it is irrelevant for the poor who are not farmers. Or, say, poor people who have managed to buy a little solar power set up. Subsidizing electricity does little for them.
Perhaps they would like that subsidy to arrive in some different manner such as help with schooling costs. Or school uniforms. Or medical care. Or transport. Being poor means there's a whole parcel of things we might consider necessities that you cannot have.
The subsidy of a thing means that politicians, or bureaucrats, or even us in a democracy, are making the choice for those poor people of what will make their lives better.
But it's a central belief of any sort of liberalism that each individual knows best what makes their own life better.
Giving them money to then spend on what they want improves their life better than giving them a subsidy on what we think they might want.
This is not something restricted to the poor. It's true of the United States right now. Most of the American system of poverty alleviation is giving poor people things. Healthcare, or vouchers for food, or vouchers to pay the rent, or a free/cheap cellphone, and on and on it goes.
Very little of that US system is just giving poor people cash. As the US census itself admits -- though you have to read fairly deeply to find it -- this makes everyone in the US poorer than they need be.
The poor value these things at less than the cost of providing these things. The poor would rather have the money, then spend that on the things that they, themselves, think makes their lives better.
We must be honest about this. It is their lives and so their opinion of what makes their life better is the only correct, or even useful, one.
We can make everyone richer by simply giving people money. For any given rise in the standard of living of the poor, as determined by those poor people, it costs less money if we just give them the cash.
Equally, for whatever amount of money we use to subsidize the poor, we increase their living standards more by just giving them the cash.
We can all have the most lovely arguments about who should be subsidized. It might even be that the answer is no one. We can similarly have arguments about how much the subsidy should be.
But it simply is true that we gain the most effect for however much money we spend upon subsidies by not trying to subsidize goods, or services, but by just giving more money to poor people.
Or, as the World Bank means but doesn't quite say -- they have to be polite -- we should subsidize people, not things. Just give poor people cash.

item.title: We need cheaper flights, not more planes
item.description:
I was indulging in a favourite Bengali pastime, watching a late-night talk show with my father, when the discussion turned to Bangladesh Biman’s plans to buy more aircraft.
The guests lamented Bangladesh’s reliance on foreign airlines, with travelers connecting through overseas hubs to reach their destinations. Their prescription was more planes of our own.
Missing from the discussion were private Bangladeshi airlines. They are ours, too. If there is substantial unmet demand, as officials claim , the government should examine what keeps private carriers from serving it.
My recent US-Bangla ticket from Chittagong to Dhaka offered one place to start. The base fare was Tk2,924. Taxes, fees, and an airline surcharge added Tk1,625, bringing the total to Tk4,549.
My ticket listed these various charges as codes. A National Skills Development Authority ticketing guide helped decode them.
IMG_5626
Passengers should pay for the airport facilities and security they use, through transparent fees tied to efficient service costs.
A broad consumption tax also has a different justification from selectively taxing flying. But the excise and travel taxes alone added Tk900, or 30.8% of the base fare.
Where did this extra tax bill come from?
The Excises and Salt Act gives the government authority to levy excise duties on specified domestic services. Fixed passenger duties take the same amount from a cheap ticket as an expensive one. An airline can cut its fare, but the duty stays put, taking a larger share of the lower price.
The government piles taxes onto tickets, discouraging sales or squeezing margins that could help finance private expansion.
Then it guarantees borrowing for Biman. The public gets a double whammy: Passengers pay more today, while taxpayers bear the risk if guaranteed debt goes unpaid. Before underwriting more aircraft, the government should reduce the tax burden and let airlines test whether passengers will support the expansion.
If officials want passengers to choose Bangladeshi airlines over foreign carriers, they should begin by making it easier for private Bangladeshi airlines to compete.
Reducing the ticket-tax burden would be one place to start: Local carriers have warned that higher duties depress demand.
These ticket taxes apply to Biman too. But government-backed borrowing changes who bears the risk of expansion.
When lenders expect the state to cover a shortfall, they have less reason to scrutinize whether new routes will pay. Managers face weaker pressure to make those investments earn their keep.
A guarantee can make aircraft easier to finance without making them commercially worthwhile. Government backing can keep resources committed to an airline that would otherwise have to improve, restructure, or relinquish them to a better operator.
Boeing has confirmed 25 aircraft ordered this year; Airbus announced ten more on October 7 .
Bangladesh may need additional capacity. Biman should still demonstrate which routes justify the investment, how debt will be repaid, and whether leasing or competing carriers could provide service more economically.
For the initial 14 Boeing aircraft, the US ambassador announced US Export-Import Bank financing. A sovereign guarantee has also been reported.
If Biman defaults on guaranteed payments, the state must meet its obligations, adding pressure for taxes, borrowing or cuts to other priorities.
CPD’s FY2026-27 budget analysis lists roughly Tk6,257 crore in Biman-related guarantees. That is contingent exposure, not an annual subsidy check or a valuation of these new orders.
If Biman fails to repay the guaranteed debt, the government must pay. Whatever it cannot recover from Biman becomes a loss for taxpayers.
What can be done?
Commercial expansion should depend on passengers buying tickets and investors accepting the risk. Before asking taxpayers to back more seats, the government should make existing seats easier to buy.
It should not impose taxes simply because it can. Each levy needs an economic justification that accounts for the costs it imposes.
Revana Sharfuddin is a research fellow at the Mercatus Centre at George Mason University.

item.title: BMU VC: Breast cancer can be cured if detected at an early stage
item.description:
Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr FM Siddiqui on Saturday said that breast cancer can be cured completely through proper treatment if it is detected at an early stage.
“Breast cancer is not only a health concern for Bangladesh but also one of the major threats to women’s health worldwide. Thousands of women in the country are affected by the disease every year,” he said. Professor Siddiqui said this at a dialogue titled “Analysis of the Global and National Situation of Breast Cancer and Ways Forward” held at the Dr Milon Hall on the BMU campus in the capital on Saturday, said a press release.
The BMU VC, however, said there is reason for hope as breast cancer is not an incurable disease. If detected at an early stage, it can be completely cured through proper treatment.
The Bangladesh Breast Cancer Awareness Forum (BBCAF) and BMU Clinical Oncology Department jointly organised the event. After the dialogue, a pink rally was brought out from the BMU campus. The rally paraded the main street from Shahbagh to Kawran Bazar and distributed awareness leaflets among the people.
BMU Clinical Oncology Department Chairman Professor Dr Syed Md Akram Hussain also spoke at the dialogue moderated by BBCAF Chief Coordinator Professor Dr Md Habibullah Talukder Ruskin.
Faculty member of Johns Hopkins University and noted public health expert Dr Halida Hanum Akhter, BMU Gynecological Oncology Department Chairman Professor Dr Jannatul Ferdous Jonaki, CCPR Chairperson Dr. Mosarrat Jahan Sourav, public health expert Dr Abu Jamil Faisal, and Founder of World Cancer Society Bangladesh Dr Syed Humayun Kabir were present, among others, at the event.

item.title: Bangladesh condemns attack on Saudi airport, seeks details of victims
item.description:
Bangladesh has strongly and unequivocally condemned the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said two Bangladeshi nationals had tragically lost their lives in the attack, while several others had been injured. Many of the injured are in critical condition.

The ministry said the Bangladesh mission in Riyadh was maintaining round-the-clock contact with the Saudi authorities to obtain detailed information about the Bangladeshi casualties and ensure that those affected received the necessary assistance.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday morning.

Houthi attack on Saudi airport kills 12 including 2 Bangladeshis, over 300 wounded

The ministry said Bangladesh extended its deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathies to the bereaved families, particularly the families of the Bangladeshi victims who had died. It also wished those injured a speedy recovery.

Bangladesh said such attacks, which endanger civilian lives and target civilian infrastructure, were unacceptable and must stop immediately.

Saudi airport attack: Five flights from Dhaka cancelled by Sunday morning

In response to the attack, Bangladesh expressed its firm solidarity with the Government of Saudi Arabia and the brotherly people of the country.

In the interests of regional peace, security and stability, Bangladesh called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and a peaceful resolution to the ongoing crisis through dialogue and diplomacy.

Saudi authorities said two Bangladeshi nationals were among the 12 people killed in an attack by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi armed group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The attack took place on Saturday and left 309 people injured.

Saudi Arabia says 3 dead at airports after Houthis claim attacks

Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a senior Houthi official, claimed responsibility for Saturday’s attack on Riyadh airport.

He said the attack was carried out in retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen. He also claimed that Saudi attacks had targeted civilian infrastructure.

This was the third attack on King Khalid International Airport this week. Following the latest incident, airport operations were temporarily suspended and all flights were diverted to other locations.

item.title: Indian capital braces for second day of protests against election chief
item.description:
INDIA-POLITICS/GEN Z

New Delhi braced for a second day of youth protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief on Sunday, as a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.

Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, and the other leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.

They were produced in front of a magistrate early on Sunday.

"Condition - no breach of peace for one year," the CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said in a post on X announcing their release.

India court releases CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke and others

Activist and social media influencer Dhruv Rathee, who was also among those detained, was released past midnight on condition he did not participate in any further protests, said an interior ministry official who declined to be named.

Police detained more than 2,000 people and locked down Delhi's city centre to thwart Saturday's protest, and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across the city on Sunday although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.

Most of those detained on the first day of protests were released late on Saturday night, police said.

Opposition parties and critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled.

India's foreign ministry said on Sunday the UN's approach was "selective" and its statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."

Millions of Names Removed from Electoral Roll

The protests are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power for more than 12 years.

Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.

The Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party.

Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

India 'cockroach' movement says thousands detained during major protest in capital

Election Commission data cited by the party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.

The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.

The cockroach party, which began as an online satire, rapidly evolved into a pressure group, with street protests against exam paper leaks culminating in the resignation of Modi's education minister.

The CJP has called its protests against Kumar "Season 2" on its social media handles, and said it would not stop until India's election system was reformed.

item.title: How Tania stopped her own child marriage
item.description:
While other students were preparing to enrol in college after completing secondary school, Tania of Satkhira was struggling to stop her own marriage. Meanwhile, the results of the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination were published. Astonishing everyone, she achieved not only a GPA of 5 but also A+ grades in every subject. She scored 100 out of 100 in chemistry and 99 in physics.

Yet she felt no joy at her remarkable achievement. Her mind was consumed by anxiety over her impending marriage and uncertainty about her future. Ultimately, thanks to the support of her teachers and her outstanding SSC results, the determined Tania managed to escape child marriage this time.

Today, Sunday, is the International Day of the Girl Child. This year’s theme is “End Child Marriage, Invest in Girls’ Rights”. The situation in Bangladesh, however, seems to tell a somewhat different story.

The latest Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) 2025, conducted by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) and UNICEF, shows that the rate of child marriage has fallen from 51.4 per cent in 2019 to 47.2 per cent. Nevertheless, among women aged 20–24, 47.2 per cent were married before turning 18, while 13.4 per cent were married before the age of 15.

The survey also found that the proportion of married women aged 15–19 rose from 32.9 per cent in 2019 to 38.9 per cent over the seven-year period. The adolescent birth rate has also increased. In 2019, there were 83 births a year for every 1,000 adolescent girls; by 2025, the figure had risen to 92.

One in every two girls subjected to child marriage

Tania’s Story

Tania Khatun is 17. Just before her SSC examinations, she learnt that a marriage proposal had come for her. Neither she nor her mother wanted the marriage, but other family members put considerable pressure on them. They cited the family’s financial hardship, concerns about girls’ safety in society and various other reasons.

Tania did not know what to do. Under pressure, she eventually said she might agree on one condition: she must be allowed to continue her education after marriage. But the prospective groom’s family refused to accept even that condition.

News of Tania’s proposed marriage spread through her school and the surrounding area. Her hopes began to fade. But the story took a turn when Tania and her mother visited Akleema Khatun, the school’s information and communication technology teacher, with sweets to celebrate Tania’s excellent results.

Tania recalled that the teacher told her mother, “She has achieved such good results. How can you marry her off like this? We have taught your daughter for five years. We also have a claim on her future.”

The teacher, along with fellow teacher Foyezul Haque and local human rights activist Sakibur Rahman, then began trying to persuade Tania’s family to abandon the marriage plan.

Eventually, they took Tania to the upazila nirbahi officer (UNO), or upazila executive officer. The UNO spoke to her family, and mounting pressure from the authorities ultimately led them to withdraw the marriage decision.

Sakibur Rahman told Prothom Alo that the greatest source of strength in Tania’s struggle was her mother, who holds a master’s degree. She had opposed the marriage from the outset. An educated mother, he said, can provide the greatest courage in such adverse circumstances.

Tania has enrolled in the first year of higher secondary education in the science stream at Satkhira Government College. Her excellent SSC results have also earned her the opportunity to receive private tuition free of charge.

I was deprived of everything: Global report hears from over 250 girls who experienced child marriage

Tania’s story is an inspiring one. But very different stories are also common. The main causes of child marriage are said to include school dropout, financial hardship within families, social customs and weak enforcement of the law. Inadequate birth registration is also seen as a major obstacle. A 2025 survey found that only 59.2 per cent of children under five had been registered at birth.

Under the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017, the minimum legal age for marriage is 18 for women and 21 for men. However, exceptions are allowed in certain circumstances. If a marriage involving a minor takes place in the best interests of the minor, with a court order and parental consent and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the rules, it is not considered an offence under the Child Marriage Restraint Act.

item.title: Many questions remain unanswered in Cumilla schoolgirl’s murder
item.description:
Police say they have solved the mystery surrounding the murder of a 15-year-old class seven student in Lalmai, Cumilla. They have arrested CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver Sumon Mia and recovered the iPhone used by the girl from a location he identified.

However, several questions remain unanswered, including why the girl was taken to an isolated paddy field via a 30-kilometre detour when her destination was just eight kilometres away, and whether anyone else was involved in the murder.

The girl’s family has lived in Cumilla for several years, so she was expected to have some familiarity with the district’s geography.

This has raised questions about how she was taken in the opposite direction instead of towards the city. According to police, Sumon Mia confessed to sexually assaulting the girl.

At a press conference at the Cumilla District Police Superintendent’s Office on Saturday morning, Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Pankaj Barua outlined the details of the high-profile murder. He said investigators had found evidence of Sumon’s involvement. The investigation is ongoing, and police have yet to establish whether anyone else was involved.

According to police, they recovered the girl’s body from a paddy field in the Uttarpara area of Bhorajagatpur in Lalmai upazila on Thursday morning. A gamchha was found around her neck. A CNG-run auto-rickshaw was parked nearby, with some clothes inside and a handbag beside it.

Driver lured schoolgirl with promise of a shortcut, then raped and killed her: Police

Police claim that when the girl tried to escape after reaching the isolated location, Sumon struggled to restrain her.

During questioning, he reportedly confessed to wrapping the gamchha around her neck and raping her. He then took her into the paddy field, forced her face down towards the ground, pressed her head down with his foot and strangled her.

According to the police investigation, the girl was looking for an auto-rickshaw to return home near the Tisha bus counter, adjacent to Noorjahan Hotel in the Padua Bazar Biswa Road area, late on Wednesday night. She boarded Sumon’s auto-rickshaw at around 12:30 am.

After negotiating the fare, Sumon agreed to take her home for Tk 300. However, instead of heading towards her home, he took the road in the opposite direction towards an isolated area.

The distance from Padua Bazar to the Racecourse area of Cumilla city is approximately eight kilometres.

According to the police account, Sumon initially drove towards Bijra Bazar along the Cumilla–Chandpur regional highway.

He then took the Cumilla–Noakhali regional highway and reached the paddy fields near Bhorajagatpur in Lalmai. The entire route covers at least 30 kilometres.

It is important to establish what happened during this lengthy detour. Vehicles travel along both regional highways at night, and some areas have at least a small number of people around. It remains unclear what the girl experienced along the route and whether she had an opportunity to seek help at any point.

According to police, Sumon claimed during questioning that the girl showed no “reaction” while the auto-rickshaw was moving.

Additional Superintendent of Police Pankaj Barua said the journey from Padua Bazar to the girl’s home should have taken no more than half an hour.

Instead, Sumon drove around for one and a half to two hours before reaching the crime scene. He said, “If the girl had called 999 at the crime scene or even before reaching it, perhaps we would not have had to witness such a death.”

Police claim that when the girl tried to escape after reaching the isolated location, Sumon struggled to restrain her.

During questioning, he reportedly confessed to wrapping the gamchha around her neck and raping her. He then took her into the paddy field, forced her face down towards the ground, pressed her head down with his foot and strangled her.

Police said the girl sent her father her “live location” at 2:58 am. Her father, who was asleep at the time, did not see the message. He noticed it towards dawn and went out to look for her.

By then, police had reached the scene and were recovering the body. He later arrived there and identified his daughter’s body.

The press conference did not provide details about the circumstances in which the girl sent her “live location”, whether she feared she was in danger at the time, or what happened after she shared it. However, the available information indicates that she still had her phone with her at that point.

CCTV footage shows a girl inside auto-rickshaw

Police said Sumon admitted to the rape allegation during questioning. However, investigators must wait for the forensic report to establish the facts conclusively. Police have also been unable to confirm whether the rape occurred before or after the murder.

CCTV footage from the area around the crime scene shows the girl sitting inside the auto-rickshaw. She appears to be seated on the rear left side.

Journalists questioned whether anyone else was in the vehicle. Police said their investigation had so far found no evidence of anyone else’s involvement apart from Sumon.

According to the police’s preliminary investigation, the girl left home on 4 October, saying she was going to visit a friend. Police later found information indicating that she had travelled to Brahmanbaria and Cox’s Bazar. She returned to Cumilla from Cox’s Bazar late on Wednesday night on an Iconic Express bus.

At around 11: 45 pm, she got off the bus in front of Noorjahan Hotel in the Padua Bazar area. She then charged her mobile phone at a shop. At around 12:15 am, she went to Padua Bazar Biswa Road and subsequently boarded an auto-rickshaw to return home, according to police.

Detailed information about how the girl travelled between different locations from 4 October until the night of 7 October has yet to emerge. Police said her family had not filed a general diary (GD) at any police station during those four days.

Following the incident, Mustain Billah Ferdous, senior assistant superintendent of police for the Cumilla Sadar South Circle, said the girl had informed her family on Wednesday afternoon that she would return home that night.

Police said Sumon left the auto-rickshaw at the crime scene after the murder and took the iPhone with him. He later bathed in a pond near Kochikata Mosque. He then travelled by another auto-rickshaw to the Bakhrabad area, where he hid the phone in bushes beside a pond. He subsequently left for Chattogram.

Police arrested him there on Friday. Acting on information he provided, police recovered the iPhone from Bakhrabad on the same day.

Questions over night-time security on highways

According to police, the incident occurred as the girl travelled home from Padua Bazar Biswa Road. The case has therefore raised questions about passenger safety and police patrols on highways and surrounding roads at night.

Earlier, on the night of 24 April, customs official Bullet Boiragi also fell into a trap set by an organised CNG-run auto-rickshaw gang after getting off a bus. The gang robbed and murdered him.

Additional Superintendent of Police Pankaj Barua said police had also identified those responsible for previous incidents and brought them to justice within 24 hours.

Meanwhile, the girl’s mother has expressed suspicions about the role of one of her daughter’s friends in her death. Speaking on Friday at the family home in Chhatiantala village in Jashore Sadar upazila, she said her daughter had told her on Wednesday afternoon that she was with a friend.

Although she asked for the friend’s name and details of her parents, her daughter did not disclose them. The mother claimed that questioning the friend could help investigators uncover information about the murder.

Additional Superintendent of Police Pankaj Barua said the investigation remained at an early stage and that investigators would seek answers to the outstanding questions as the inquiry progressed.

item.title: Saudi airport attack: Five flights from Dhaka cancelled by Sunday morning
item.description:
A total of five flights from Dhaka had been cancelled by Sunday morning because King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh, was closed. One of them was a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight on the Dhaka–Riyadh route. Flights operated by various Saudi Arabian airlines were also cancelled.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the flights were cancelled because the airport was closed. Biman Bangladesh Airlines informed about the cancellation of its flight from last night.

Houthi attack on Saudi airport kills 12 including 2 Bangladeshis, over 300 wounded

The cancelled flights included Saudia Airlines flights SV 804 and SV 805, SV 806 and SV 807, and RX 763 and RX 764. Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG 339, which was scheduled to fly from Dhaka to Riyadh, was also cancelled.

On Saturday, US-Bangla Airlines flight BS 381 was unable to reach its destination and landed elsewhere. It was scheduled to arrive in Dhaka at 3:10 pm on Saturday but landed at 3:10 am early on Sunday.

In an urgent notice issued on Saturday, Biman Bangladesh Airlines said all flights from Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport had been suspended.

As a result, the airline suspended flights BG 339 and BG 340 on the Dhaka–Riyadh–Dhaka route. Passengers who had booked tickets on the two flights were advised not to go to the airport.

Biman said it was monitoring the situation and would officially announce the latest flight status and revised schedules.

The disruption and changes to flight schedules caused by the situation at Riyadh airport have left passengers facing difficulties. The authorities have advised passengers to contact their respective airlines and check the latest status of their flights before heading to the airport.

Evacuations, injuries at Riyadh airport after alleged Houthi attack

According to flight-tracking website Flightradar24, all flights bound for Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled. A Reuters report said the decision was taken following an explosion at the international airport in the Saudi capital on Saturday.

Reuters, reporting the suspension of flights at Riyadh’s international airport, said the airport authorities had asked passengers to contact their respective airlines before travelling there. They were also advised to check the latest status of their flights.

In addition to the cancellations, Biman issued a notice on Saturday night announcing the suspension of flights BG 339 and BG 340 until further notice. Both flights operate on the Dhaka–Riyadh–Dhaka route.

item.title: Wholesale market on hospital land
item.description:
A wholesale market is being built on a piece of land in Ashulia, Dhaka, earmarked for a private medical college. Local residents say the construction of the market amounts to a permanent takeover of the land, making it unlikely that a medical college will ever be built there.

The land where the market is being built belonged to Kamar Para School and College. According to local sources and documents, in 2010 the school’s then management committee allocated 164 decimals of its land for a medical college. The proposed institution was to be named Uttara Bangabandhu Medical College and Hospital.

Local residents say the Awami League was politically dominant at the time and wanted to establish the medical college under Bangabandhu’s name. After the July mass uprising, Awami League leaders left the area, and Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leaders and activists took control of everything. The wholesale market, they allege, is being built to serve the personal interests of those involved.

Kamar Para School and College was established in 1977 at the initiative of a club called Harirampur Cultural Association. The club is no longer active, although a few of its members are still alive. None of them agreed to speak officially.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, one member said the area lacked a good healthcare facility, which was why the initiative had been taken to build a hospital and medical college on the school’s land. During the Awami League’s tenure, the proposed hospital was named after Bangabandhu to help secure approval. Now, the BNP has taken over the very land intended for the hospital, the member said.

The proposed hospital site lies on the right-hand side of the road towards Ashulia, after Kamar Para bus stand in the capital’s Turag police station area. On 4 October, a visit to Kamar Para found construction of a wholesale market for fresh produce in full swing. A large section of the boundary wall had been demolished to make way for the market. A banner on the wall read: “Wholesale Market for Fresh Produce — Shops Available for Allocation.”

Stalls for the market were being built with bamboo and corrugated tin sheets. Around 50 workers were on site. When asked who had commissioned the construction, the workers declined to comment.

At around 11:30 am on 8 October, Prothom Alo photojournalist Sazid Hossain went to photograph the vegetable wholesale market on the hospital land. As he approached, he saw five people beating a man. The attackers were heard telling the victim, “If you say anything more about this work, we’ll kill you.”

Sazid moved a short distance away and began taking photographs with a drone. At one point, several people supervising the market’s construction rushed towards him. He then left the area on his motorcycle.

Earlier Attempts to Take Over the Land

After the Awami League fell from power on 5 August 2024, Zahirul Islam, joint convener of the BNP’s Turag unit, occupied the proposed hospital site and set up a truck stand.

Zahirul said he had not acted alone and that another group had also been involved. “I operated the stand for three months. During that time, I also paid money to Kamar Para School,” he said.

Following criticism, Zahirul was forced to remove the truck stand. The current wholesale market is being built by a company called Rafiq Engineering and Construction. Its director, Rafiqul Islam, told Prothom Alo that he was carrying out the work after renting the land. The monthly rent is Tk 1.6 million.

Several local sources said that although Rafiq’s company had formally rented the land, the arrangement was essentially a political settlement, with Zahirul Islam, joint convener of the BNP’s Turag unit, playing a role behind the scenes. 

Zahirul had also participated in the tender to rent the land but had not been awarded the contract. Given the limited scope for proceeding without reaching an understanding with him, the sources said, Rafiq’s company had negotiated an arrangement with Zahirul.

“It is a political undertaking, so we have to work with everyone,” Rafiqul said.

Zahirul, a Turag BNP leader, is a follower of Mostafa Zaman, member-secretary of the BNP’s Dhaka North City unit. The party recently dissolved that committee following an attack and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre, a maternal and child healthcare facility in Mirpur, Dhaka.

Mostafa Zaman is also the president of the governing body of Kamar Para School and College. Local sources said he controls the school and arranged for the land to be rented out. Those who rented it are his followers, creating opportunities for mutual benefit, they alleged.

When contacted, Mostafa Zaman said the college principal would speak on the matter. When asked about his own involvement, he ended the call.

Principal Khurshid Jahan was absent from the college for a long period after the July mass uprising. Sources said she was able to return on the condition that she agreed to the land being rented out. Asked why the land had been leased for a wholesale market rather than a hospital, she said the decision had been made in the school’s best interests.

After construction of the wholesale market began, local BNP leader Biplab Hossain posted a Facebook Live video on 26 September urging other party leaders and activists to join the work. He introduced himself as a joint convener of the BNP’s Turag unit.

In the video, Biplab said, “All the leaders of the Turag BNP unit should come here. We will all stay together and work together.”

The video showed at least 20 people, including local BNP leader Zahirul.

Questions Over the Rental Arrangement

Ownership of the school’s land was transferred to the medical college in 2010. Mohammad Bayezid Sardar, assistant commissioner (land) at the Mirpur Revenue Circle, told Prothom Alo, “According to our records, the land is still registered in the name of Uttara Bangabandhu Medical College and Hospital. However, we cannot say who is currently occupying it.”

This raises questions about whether the school authorities have the right to rent out land registered in the name of a hospital. Several members of Harirampur Cultural Association, the organisation behind the school and the proposed medical college, said the entire process had been carried out illegally through the abuse of political power. They estimated the land to be worth at least Tk 1 billion and alleged that the site was effectively being taken over under the guise of establishing a wholesale market.

At noon on 4 October, Mukul Ahmed was walking past the grounds of the proposed Kamar Para Medical College. When asked about the development, he told Prothom Alo, “I knew a hospital would be built here. It would have benefited us. Now, I don’t think the hospital will ever be built.”

item.title: Messi nets brace to win in first match after Argentina exit
item.description:
SOCCER-USA/

Lionel Messi scored twice to help Inter Miami rout DC United 4-0 on Saturday, taking a victory in his first match since saying farewell to the Argentina national team.

Four nights after scoring in his final match for the Albiceleste in a victory over Benin, the 39-year-old South American superstar struck in the 47th and 60th minutes as defending MLS champion Miami won for only the second time in their past 11 league matches.

A first-half brace by Luis Suarez staked the Herons to the lead as they improved to 13-5 with 10 drawn for 49 points, jumping from third to second in the Eastern Conference

Emotion, tears as Messi retires from Argentina national team

Messi hopes to make Miami the first team to win back-to-back MLS crowns since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011-12.

Messi, the top point producer in the league with 23 goals plus assists on 13 others, seeks a third consecutive MLS Most Valuable Player award.

Uruguayan striker Suarez scored in the third minute to give Miami the lead, blasting a left-footed shot from the heart of the box into the top left corner.

Suarez struck again in the 39th for his 16th goal of the campaign, assisted like his first of the night by German Berterame.

Messi plays ‘The Last Tango’ for the Albiceleste in photos

Messi blasted home a left-footed shot off an assist from Suarez to give Miami a 3-0 lead and evaded three defenders to add another goal 13 minutes later as the pink-clad hosts pulled away to stay.

In other games, Scottish striker Lewis Morgan and American Djordje Mihailovic scored in second-half stoppage time to rally Toronto for a 2-1 home victory over Montreal.

The visitors grabbed the lead in the Canadian clash on a goal by Mexican forward Daniel Rios in the 52nd minute.

Toronto, however, battled back for the equalizer by winger Morgan, obtained last month from San Diego, in the third minute of stoppage time, his first regular-season MLS goal in two years.

Ronaldo hails Messi after Argentina great says he already misses national team

Former Montreal standout Mihailovic struck for the decider in the fifth minute of extra time.

"Now I've scored on both sides of this derby," he said. "It feels good."

Toronto snapped a three-game losing streak to pull within a point of an East playoff berth.

At Chicago, Swiss forward Maren Haile-Selassie scored in the 87th minute to give the 10-man Chicago Fire a 2-1 triumph over New York City.

Austrian midfielder Hannes Wolf gave City the lead in the 19th minute and Chicago dropped to 10 men when Ivory coast midfielder Dje D'Avilla received his second yellow card in the 43rd minute.

Swede Anton Saletros equalized for Chicago in the 55th minute, setting the stage for the decider.

item.title: 2 Bangladeshis among 12 killed in Riyadh airport attack
item.description:
At least 12 people, including two Bangladeshis, were killed and 309 injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, according to the country’s civil aviation authority, Al Jazeera reported.
In a statement issued early Sunday, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said the fatalities included four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one citizen each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.
Some of the injured are in critical condition and are receiving treatment at hospitals, the authority said. The attack also caused property damage, the extent of which is still being assessed.
GACA had earlier announced the temporary suspension of airport operations following the attack as officials assessed the damage and casualties.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthi rebels blamed the group for the attack on the airport’s passenger terminal, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime”.
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki Al-Maliki said a decisive response would be delivered in accordance with international humanitarian law.
Al-Maliki also reported a separate incident involving a projectile that struck an area near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio strongly condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including the strike on King Khalid International Airport. The Houthis had not claimed responsibility for Saturday’s attack at the time of the report.
In a post on social media platform X on Saturday, Rubio said the attacks showed disregard for civilian lives and must stop immediately.
According to GACA, at least three Saudi nationals, including a pilot, were killed in an attack on King Khalid International Airport on Thursday.
Al Jazeera correspondent Youssef Mawry, reporting from Yemen on Saturday, said the Houthis had yet to claim responsibility for the latest attack.
However, the Iran-backed group had warned airlines to avoid Saudi airspace, saying aircraft flying through the country’s airspace, except over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, could become targets.
Following reports of the latest attack, US President Donald Trump was asked by reporters outside the White House whether Washington would join Saudi Arabia in striking the Houthis.
“We might. We will look into it. I just learned about the recent attack, so we will make a decision soon. We act very quickly,” he said.
Meanwhile, the embassies of several countries in Riyadh, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada, issued advisories urging their citizens in Saudi Arabia to exercise caution and avoid the airport.

item.title: Bangladesh strongly condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
item.description:
Bangladesh on Sunday strongly and unequivocally condemned Saturday’s deadly Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people, including two Bangladeshi nationals, and injured more than 300 others, many of them critically.
The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is in contact with the Saudi authorities to ascertain details of the deceased and injured Bangladeshis and to facilitate necessary assistance to those affected.
Bangladesh extended its deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathies to the bereaved families, including the families of the Bangladeshi victims, and prays for the swift and full recovery of all those injured.
"Attacks endangering civilian lives and targeting civilian infrastructure are unacceptable and must cease immediately," said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in a statement.
Bangladesh reiterated its firm solidarity with the government and the brotherly people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the face of this attack.
Bangladesh called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and a peaceful resolution of the ongoing crisis through dialogue and diplomacy, in the interest of regional peace, security and stability.
A missile attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people, including two Bangladeshis, and injured more than 300 others, Saudi civil aviation authorities said on Sunday, with several victims in critical condition.
The Saudi-led coalition blamed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen for the attack, calling the strike a “fully-fledged war crime” and vowing a firm response, reports AP.
The fatalities also included four Saudi citizens, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese national.
